transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Could you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess what brings me in is this restless feeling that just doesn’t seem to shut off. Like I’m wound too tight most of the time, even when I’m supposed to be sitting calmly in a planning meeting at work, or when I’m painting—which is supposed to be relaxing—or even doing yoga. I’ll be there trying to settle, and my body just feels like it’s ready to jump up and do something else.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things, even when there isn’t much going on, or feeling like your anxiety is hard to control?

I’m not sure I’d call it worry exactly. I mean, I do think about things—work stuff, orders, whether I remembered to follow up with someone—but I don’t know if it’s that “can’t control anxiety” kind of thing. Sometimes I’ll start thinking about one thing and then suddenly I’m remembering I need to buy dog food or that I never returned a sweater, and then I’m off making a list in my head. So… I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed it as constant worry, if that makes sense.
Do you find it hard to focus on tasks, even when you’re not anxious, or do you get easily distracted by things around you or your own thoughts?

Yeah, I do get distracted, but the thing I notice more is mistakes in details. Like at work, over the last couple years, I’ll swear I checked a vendor spreadsheet carefully—really checked it—and then our planning coordinator will catch something like I transposed a SKU, or I missed a freight surcharge, or I copied the wrong quantity into the purchase order.

And it’s frustrating because I’m not trying to rush, exactly… well, sometimes everything is moving fast in buying, especially around seasonal stuff, and then I start thinking about one vendor while I’m looking at another one’s sheet—but anyway, yes, even when I’m not feeling anxious, my focus can slip and then these little errors show up.
Have you noticed feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like painting or other activities?

I don’t think so… not in a big way. I mean, I still like painting once I actually get myself set up, though sometimes I spend more time rearranging the brushes than painting, which is ridiculous because I have this one jar I keep meaning to replace—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

I haven’t really noticed feeling down or sad most of the time. It’s more like I get irritated with myself, but I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest in the things I enjoy.
Do you often feel the need to move around, tap your feet, or fidget when you're trying to sit still, like you just can't stay in one place for long?

Yeah… I think so. Especially on supplier calls. I’ll be sitting there trying to listen and my foot is just bouncing under the desk the whole time, or I’m clicking a pen without realizing it. Sometimes I’m twisting my ring over and over, and then I notice I’m doing it on video and I’ll move my hands out of view or mute myself if the pen is making noise. It’s not like I’m trying to be distracting, it just sort of happens when I have to sit still.
Do these feelings of restlessness and difficulty focusing happen in different parts of your life, like at home, at work, and in social situations, or are they mostly limited to certain places?

It’s definitely not just one place. Work is where it shows up the most clearly, because there’s a paper trail, you know? Like purchase orders get corrected, or my planning coordinator has to do this extra review because I missed something, and then I feel embarrassed because I really did look at it.

At home it’s different. It’s more… at family dinners, I’ll jump in or talk over people without meaning to, and then the mood gets tense. Someone will say, “Can I finish?” and I’m like, oh, I didn’t even realize I was doing it. So yes, it’s in more than one setting, not just work.

When did you first start noticing these kinds of issues with restlessness, focus, or making mistakes in details? Were they something you experienced even as a child, like before you were 12 years old?

Yeah, I think it goes back pretty far. I remember in elementary school getting notes sent home because I kept popping out of my seat or talking over other kids. And I’d do this thing where I’d answer before the teacher even finished asking the question, because I was so sure I knew it—or I just couldn’t wait, I guess.

My mom kept some of those notes for years in this folder with report cards and school photos, which is funny because she was very organized about that kind of thing… but yes, before 12, definitely.
